q: In both DAEDS and DADS arrangements under SPP Doc. 202, what happens to the professional responsibility and civil liability of each State-regulated professional (Architect and other RLPs) involved in the project?
o: The professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each professional remain separate; the Architect does not assume the responsibilities/liabilities of the other RLPs
The Architect assumes full liability for all other professionals in both cases
Liability is transferred entirely to the Owner once the contract is signed
Liability is pooled and shared equally among all professionals regardless of contract structure
n: Sec. 6.1 states that in both DAEDS and DADS, the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate, and the Architect does not assume the responsibilities and liabilities of the other RLPs. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: An Architect designing a Group II parish church wants to hold a single, sole contract with the Owner, personally engaging and sub-contracting the structural and electrical engineers under her own agreements. Which arrangement should the Service Agreement specify?
o: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS)
n: DAEDS is defined precisely as a single contract between the Architect and the Owner, with the Architect entering sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals — matching the Architect's intended arrangement here. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: Which of the following is listed under Group II as a residential-type building distinct from the single-family residences of Group IV?
n: Residential Condominiums is listed under Group II, while single-detached/single-attached/duplex residences, row-houses and shop-houses, small apartment houses, and townhouses fall under Group 4. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2; SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: In the formula used to compute this project's DAEDS fee, what does the 'P3,000,000' base amount represent?
o: A fixed government filing fee unrelated to PCC
The RPF that would already be earned at the P50.0-million bracket boundary, per the 6% Group II DAEDS rate
A minimum professional fee mandated by law regardless of bracket
50% of the total project construction cost
n: The P3,000,000 base is simply 6% of P50,000,000 — the DAEDS fee already accrued up to the bracket boundary — to which 5% of the excess above P50M is then added. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A Group II shopping center is being designed with a PCC of P75,000,000.00, which falls in the 'Over P50.0 million to P100.0 million' bracket.

q: Compute the Group II DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A proposed Group II retail/wholesale store complex has a PCC of P235,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P200.0 million to P500.0 million' bracket.

q: Which of the following building types is explicitly classified under Group II in SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2?
n: Fire Stations is one of the enumerated Group II building types. Manufacturing/Industrial Plants, Hangars, and Public Markets are all Group 1 (simplest) buildings. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2; SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1)

q: A property developer asks the Architect to itemize the professional fee for a proposed Group II mall complex using a flat percentage of the estimated construction budget, rather than a per-diem or lump-sum arrangement. Which method of compensation under Sec. 6.2 is being used, and which section's bracket table should the Architect apply given the building type?
o: Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method; Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4)
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses method; Sec. 6.3.3 (Group 3)
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method; Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1)
Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost method; Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2)
n: A flat percentage of the estimated construction budget is the Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost method (Sec. 6.2.1); since a mall complex is a Group II building type, the Sec. 6.3.2 bracket table applies. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.2; SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Why does SPP Document 202 group buildings into categories such as Group I, Group II, and Group III at all?
o: To determine which professionals are legally allowed to design the building
To determine the fair remuneration of the Architect according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required by the building type
To determine the government agency with jurisdiction over the project
To determine the required number of construction permits
n: Sec. 6.2 explains that professional architectural work is classified according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required, and 'a grouping of buildings is provided to determine the fair remuneration for the Architect.' (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.2)

q: Relative to Group I (simplest buildings) and Group III (exceptional buildings), where does Group II sit in the overall SPP Doc. 202 fee-schedule hierarchy?
o: Between Group I and Group III — its RPF percentages at every PCC bracket are higher than Group I's but lower than Group III's
Group II is not comparable because it uses a flat fee rather than a percentage schedule
Below Group I in required design complexity and fee percentage
Above Group III in required design complexity and fee percentage
n: Group I's DAEDS base rate is 5% (≤50M), Group II's is 6%, and Group III's is 7% — the fee schedule escalates with design complexity from Group I through Group III, placing Group II in the middle. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1; SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2; SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee at this exact PCC?
n: At exactly P50.0 million, the PCC still falls in the '≤P50.0 million' bracket at 6%: 6% x P50,000,000 = P3,000,000.00 — which is also the fixed base amount used to start the next bracket (Over P50M to P100M). (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged for a Group II project — a private club building — with a PCC of exactly P50,000,000.00 (the upper boundary of the first fee bracket).

q: An Architect is asked to design a proposed nursing home with a PCC of P90,000,000.00 under a DAEDS arrangement. Which bracket of the Group II fee table applies, and what fixed base amount does the computation start from?
o: The Over P200M-P500M bracket, starting from a P9,500,000 base
The Over P100M-P200M bracket, starting from a P5,500,000 base
The Over P50M-P100M bracket, starting from a P3,000,000 base
n: P90,000,000 falls between P50.0 million and P100.0 million, so the applicable DAEDS formula is P3,000,000 plus 5% of the excess over P50.0 million. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A nursing home project (Group II) has a PCC of P90,000,000.00.

q: Compute the Group II DADS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A Group II mixed-use building has a PCC of P700,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion' bracket.

q: How much MORE does the Architect earn under a DAEDS arrangement than under a DADS arrangement for this P235,000,000.00 project?
n: DAEDS RPF (P10,550,000.00) minus DADS RPF (P6,330,000.00) = P4,220,000.00 — the additional compensation for the Architect's coordination of and single-contract responsibility for the sub-consultancy engineering/allied professional services under DAEDS. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A proposed Group II retail/wholesale store complex has a PCC of P235,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P200.0 million to P500.0 million' bracket.

q: Postal facilities, police stations, and welfare buildings share which classification under SPP Doc. 202's building-type groups?
n: Postal Facilities, Police Stations, and Welfare Buildings are all explicitly enumerated Group II building types under Sec. 6.3.2. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: What is the DAEDS 'excess' percentage rate applied above the P1.0-billion threshold for Group II projects, and how does it compare to the base (≤P50M) rate?
n: Sec. 6.3.2's Group II DAEDS table applies 1% to the excess of PCC over P1.0 billion, versus the 6% base rate applied to PCC of P50.0 million and less — the marginal percentage rate declines as PCC grows. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A large Group II serviced-apartment / condominium development has a PCC of P1,500,000,000.00 (P1.5 billion), placing it in the 'Over P1.0 billion' bracket.

q: Group II buildings are informally described in architecture board-exam reviewers by which single word, reflecting their design complexity relative to Groups I and III?
n: Group 1 buildings are of the 'simplest' character, Group 2 buildings require a 'moderate' amount of research and design effort, and Group 3 buildings are of 'exceptional' character and complexity — Group 2 sits between the two. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1; SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2; SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: Under Sec. 6.1 of SPP Doc. 202, what distinguishes Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) from Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS)?
o: DAEDS covers only residential projects while DADS covers commercial projects
DAEDS excludes engineering design entirely while DADS includes it

In DAEDS the Architect holds a single contract with the Owner and sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals; in DADS the Architect and the other professionals each contract directly and separately with the Owner
DAEDS is used only for Group I buildings while DADS is used only for Group II buildings
n: Sec. 6.1.1 defines DAEDS as a single Architect-Owner contract with the Architect sub-contracting the allied professionals, while Sec. 6.1.2 defines DADS as the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals each having separate direct contracts with the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: A publishing plant, an exhibition hall, and a laundry/cleaning facility are all being planned in the same city. Under SPP Doc. 202, how does the fee schedule classify all three?
o: Publishing plants are Group I, exhibition halls are Group II, and laundries are Group III
n: Publishing Plants, Exhibition Halls & Display Structures, and Laundries & Cleaning Facilities are all explicitly listed under Group II in Sec. 6.3.2. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Percentage of Project Construction Cost (PCC) is one method of computing the Architect's Recommended Professional Fee under SPP Doc. 202. Under which specific subsection is this method first named?
n: Sec. 6.2.1 names 'Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost (PCC)' as one of the methods of compensation for Regular Design Services; the Group 1-10 bracket tables (e.g., Sec. 6.3.2 for Group 2) apply this method. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.2)

q: An Owner wants to contract the structural engineer directly and separately, rather than have the Architect sub-contract that engineer. Which manner of providing Regular Design Services should the parties use for a Group II project?
o: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS)
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses arrangement
n: Under DADS, the Architect and each of the engineering and allied professionals execute separate contracts directly with the Owner, matching the Owner's stated preference. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a Group II building type in Sec. 6.3.2?
n: Convention Facilities is listed under Group III (exceptional), not Group II. Correctional & Detention Facilities, Court Houses/Halls of Justice, and Convents/Monasteries/Seminaries are all Group II. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2; SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.3)

q: 'Other buildings of similar nature or use' appears at the end of the Group II building list in Sec. 6.3.2. What is the function of this catch-all phrase?
o: It extends Group II classification, by analogy, to building types not individually named but comparable in complexity/use to those enumerated
It refers only to buildings constructed after the document's 2016 effectivity date
It voids the rest of the list, making the group open to any building type whatsoever
It restricts Group II to only the buildings explicitly named, with no room for analogous types
n: The 'other buildings of similar nature or use' clause allows building types not specifically named in the list to be classified by analogy to the enumerated Group II examples, based on comparable moderate design complexity. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Why does the Recommended Professional Fee percentage for DAEDS exceed that for DADS at every Project Construction Cost bracket, for the same building group?
o: DAEDS fees include a mandatory profit markup not present in DADS
There is no real difference; the two schedules are numerically identical

Under DAEDS the Architect's single fee also compensates for coordinating and being responsible for the sub-consultancy contracts with the engineering and allied professionals, which DADS excludes because those professionals contract and are paid directly by the Owner
DADS is a discounted promotional rate offered only to government projects
n: Because DAEDS bundles the architectural and engineering/allied design services into one Architect-held contract, its RPF percentage is higher than DADS, which covers architectural design services alone. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: Compute the Group II DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee for this project.
n: DAEDS for this bracket = P3,000,000 + [5% x (PCC - P50M)] = P3,000,000 + [5% x P25,000,000] = P3,000,000 + P1,250,000 = P4,250,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A Group II shopping center is being designed with a PCC of P75,000,000.00, which falls in the 'Over P50.0 million to P100.0 million' bracket.

q: Using the Group II DADS bracket schedule instead, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: For PCC of P50.0 million and less, the Group II DADS rate is a flat 3.6% of PCC: 3.6% x P30,000,000 = P1,080,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under a Group II project — a proposed 4-storey office building — with a Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P30,000,000.00.

q: A city government is planning a new City Hall / Civic Center. Under SPP Doc. 202, which building-type group governs its Recommended Professional Fee?
n: City/Town Halls & Civic Centers are explicitly enumerated under Group II in Sec. 6.3.2. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Which of the following pairs of building types are BOTH explicitly enumerated under Group II?
n: Banks, Exchange and Other Financial Institutions, and Churches and Religious Facilities, are both listed under Group II. Airports/Hotels are Group 3; Armories/Bakeries are Group 1; Museums/Mausoleums are Group 5. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: An Architect is engaged to design a private social club (Group II) with an estimated PCC of P480,000,000.00 under a DADS arrangement. Which bracket applies, and what is the correct base fixed amount to use before adding the marginal percentage?
o: Over P500M-P1B bracket; base of P11,100,000, plus 1.2% of the excess over P500M
Over P200M-P500M bracket; base of P5,700,000, plus 1.8% of the excess over P200M
Over P50M-P100M bracket; base of P1,800,000, plus 3.0% of the excess over P50M
Over P100M-P200M bracket; base of P3,300,000, plus 2.4% of the excess over P100M
n: P480,000,000 falls between P200.0 million and P500.0 million, so the Group II DADS formula is P5,700,000 plus 1.8% of the excess over P200.0 million. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A private club project (Group II) has a PCC of P480,000,000.00, to be delivered under DADS.

q: Compute the Group II DADS Recommended Professional Fee for the same project.
scenario: A proposed Group II retail/wholesale store complex has a PCC of P235,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P200.0 million to P500.0 million' bracket.

q: A proposed college dormitory building would be classified under which SPP Doc. 202 building-type group for purposes of computing the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Dormitories are explicitly listed among the Group II (moderate complexity) building types in Sec. 6.3.2. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: What is the defining characteristic of Building Type Group II under SPP Document 202's Regular Design Services fee schedule?
o: Buildings of exceptional character and complexity of plan/design requiring comparatively large amounts of research
Buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design requiring a moderate amount of research and of engineering and allied architectural design
Buildings of the simplest utilization and character, without complication of plan/design
Monumental buildings requiring consummate design skill and much precise detailing
n: Sec. 6.3.2 defines Group 2 as buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design requiring a moderate amount of research and of engineering and allied architectural design — hence the informal label 'Moderate.' (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Compute the Group II DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A Group II multi-storey apartment building has a PCC of P150,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P100.0 million to P200.0 million' bracket.

scenario: A large Group II serviced-apartment / condominium development has a PCC of P1,500,000,000.00 (P1.5 billion), placing it in the 'Over P1.0 billion' bracket.

q: A bowling alley (bowlodrome) and a call center are both being fitted out in the same commercial building. For fee-computation purposes under SPP Doc. 202, both uses fall under:
n: Bowlodromes and Call Centers are both explicitly listed Group II building types in Sec. 6.3.2. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Compute the Group II DADS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A Group II multi-storey apartment building has a PCC of P150,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P100.0 million to P200.0 million' bracket.

q: Compute the Group II DADS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A large Group II serviced-apartment / condominium development has a PCC of P1,500,000,000.00 (P1.5 billion), placing it in the 'Over P1.0 billion' bracket.

q: The building-type group classification system (Groups 1 through 10) under which section of SPP Document 202 is used to determine the Recommended Professional Fee for Regular Design Services?
n: Sec. 6.3, 'Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)', groups buildings (Groups 1-10, with Group 2 defined in Sec. 6.3.2) to determine the fair remuneration of the Architect based on design complexity. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3)

q: A supermarket/hypermarket, a shopping mall, and a retail store are each being designed as separate projects. Under SPP Doc. 202, how are all three classified?
o: All three fall under Group II
They are classified differently depending on floor area
All three fall under Group III
All three fall under Group I
n: Supermarkets/Hyper-marts, Malls/Mall Complexes, and Retail/Wholesale Stores are all explicitly listed under Group II — classification under SPP Doc. 202 is by building type/use, not by floor area. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: What is the DADS Recommended Professional Fee at this exact PCC?
n: At exactly P50.0 million, the PCC still falls in the '≤P50.0 million' bracket at 3.6%: 3.6% x P50,000,000 = P1,800,000.00 — the fixed base for the next DADS bracket. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged for a Group II project — a private club building — with a PCC of exactly P50,000,000.00 (the upper boundary of the first fee bracket).

q: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a Group II building type under SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2?
n: Office Buildings / Office Condominium is one of the enumerated Group II building types. Public Markets and Warehouses are Group 1 (simplest) buildings, while Hospitals & Medical Buildings are Group 3 (exceptional). (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)

q: Compute the Group II DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee.
scenario: A Group II mixed-use building has a PCC of P700,000,000.00, placing it in the 'Over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion' bracket.

q: Compute the Group II DADS Recommended Professional Fee for this same project.
n: DADS for this bracket = P1,800,000 + [3.0% x (PCC - P50M)] = P1,800,000 + [3.0% x P25,000,000] = P1,800,000 + P750,000 = P2,550,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: A Group II shopping center is being designed with a PCC of P75,000,000.00, which falls in the 'Over P50.0 million to P100.0 million' bracket.

q: Using the Group II DAEDS bracket schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: For PCC of P50.0 million and less, the Group II DAEDS rate is a flat 6% of PCC: 6% x P30,000,000 = P1,800,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), Sec. 6.3.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under a Group II project — a proposed 4-storey office building — with a Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P30,000,000.00.
